title: Simple perverse sheaves on a smooth curve
statement:
In the setting and with the conventions of [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart],
the simple objects of the abelian category $\mathrm{Perv}(C)$ are the
following:

- the *punctual* objects $i_{x*}E$ (in degree $0$), where $x$ is a closed
  point of $C$ and $E$ is an irreducible sheaf on $x$, that is, an
  irreducible Weil module at $x$ in the Weil case;
- the *middle extensions* $(j_*\mathcal N)[1]$ of [def-wf-middle-extension],
  where $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ is a dense open immersion and $\mathcal N$
  is a nonzero irreducible lisse sheaf on $U$. Here irreducible means that
  $\mathcal N$ has no lisse subsheaf other than $0$ and $\mathcal N$.

Every object of either kind is simple, and every simple object is of one
of these kinds.

external.place: We also use [lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective] (SGA 1, Exposé V, Proposition 8.2): for a dense open $k:U'\hookrightarrow U$ of a smooth curve, the maps of fundamental groups and of Weil groups are surjective, and consequently, for a lisse sheaf $\mathcal N$ on $U$, the unit $\mathcal N\to k_*k^*\mathcal N$ is an isomorphism (part (3)) and, if $\mathcal N$ is irreducible, so is $k^*\mathcal N$ (par

proof.text: Use exactly the perfect-field, smooth separated finite-type pure-dimension-one curve and rational coefficient conventions of [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart]. Work first in its geometric category; the Weil interpretation is justified in Step 4. All sheaves below are in the standard constructible heart. By [sk-lem-coefficient-heart], a constructible sheaf is lisse on a dense open; finitely many such opens have a common dense intersection. A dense open of our curve contains every component generic point, so its closed complement has dimension at most zero and is a finite set of closed points by [lem-sc-dim0-finite]. Thus a sheaf vanishing on that open is punctual. We use exact restrictions, the ordinary adjunction $j^*\dashv j_*$, and the exact fully faithful closed direct image from [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology]. In particular these operations remain in the same rational coefficient category; no comparison with discrete coefficient sheaves is being assumed.

source.place: Opening conventions; common lisse opens used in the middle-extension and classification paragraphs

proof.text: Here is the precise dense-restriction input used below. Smooth curves are normal by [lem-sc-smooth-normal]. On each connected component of a lisse open $V$, [lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective](1) makes $\pi_1(V')\to\pi_1(V)$ surjective for a dense open $V'$. Under the exact fibre equivalence [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2), the two actions consequently have exactly the same invariant subspaces and intertwining linear maps: invariance or commutation for the image is invariance or commutation for the whole group. Thus restriction is fully faithful and gives a bijection on lisse subobjects. The same conclusion holds on a finite disjoint union by applying it on each component. For Weil sheaves, use [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]: a subobject on the geometric open extends component by component; its Frobenius isomorphism extends uniquely by full faithfulness, as does its inverse, and the inclusion is equivariant because this can be tested on the dense open. Therefore restriction also gives a bijection on Weil lisse subobjects. In particular it preserves and reflects irreducibility. The ordinary unit $M\to v_*v^*M$ for lisse $M$ is an isomorphism componentwise by [lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective](3), and its naturality makes it a Weil isomorphism when applicable.

source.place: Opening paragraph: dense-open monodromy and the lisse unit; stated componentwise to avoid a geometric-connectedness assumption

proof.text: Two elementary consequences of [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart](3),(4) and [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology] will be used repeatedly. If $M$ is lisse and $j$ is a dense open immersion, $(j_*M)[1]$ belongs to the heart, so $j_*M$ has no nonzero punctual subsheaf. Taking $j$ to be the identity gives the same assertion for $M$. If a constructible sheaf $F$ has no punctual subsheaf and $v$ is a dense open on which $F$ is lisse, exactness of $v^*$ and $v^*v_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ show that the kernel of $F\to v_*v^*F$ is supported on the finite complement. Hence that kernel is zero, and this unit is monic. A subsheaf of a sheaf with no punctual subsheaf again has none, since a punctual subobject would compose to one of the original sheaf.

source.place: Middle-extension paragraph (a), and the unit in the classification paragraph

proof.text: For the Weil case, all these constructions are on the geometric fiber with Frobenius pairs as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Pullback by Frobenius preserves the ordinary and perverse classes described in [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart]; it is an exact autoequivalence of each geometric heart. The kernel of an equivariant morphism has a unique induced Frobenius isomorphism, because applying that autoequivalence to its kernel diagram gives another kernel diagram. The same argument applies to cokernels. Therefore a sequence of equivariant maps in either heart is exact if and only if its underlying sequence is exact. In particular, below we apply [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] only in the geometric derived category. When the resulting first two maps are equivariant, the last map inherits its equivariance from the cokernel universal property, so the short exact sequence is also one of Weil perverse pairs. This does not put a triangulated structure on the fixed-pair category. Common lisse opens may be chosen over $k_0$: the maximal lisse locus is Frobenius-stable, and its finite complement descends; finite intersections and removing punctual supports preserve this property.

source.place: All Weil versions of the source proof: exact sequences are interpreted in the fixed-pair heart

proof.text:
Let $E$ be irreducible on a closed point $x$, and let $0\to Q\to i_{x*}E\to R\to0$ be exact in the perverse heart. By [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart](5), $\mathcal H^{-1}Q=0$ and
$$0\to\mathcal H^{-1}R\to\mathcal H^0Q\to i_{x*}E\to\mathcal H^0R\to0.$$
The first sheaf is a punctual subsheaf of the punctual $\mathcal H^0Q$, and has no punctual subsheaf by part (3), so it is zero. Thus $\mathcal H^0Q$ is a subsheaf of $i_{x*}E$. Apply [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology] to the complement of $x$: exact $i_x^*$ and fully faithful $i_{x*}$ identify sheaves supported at $x$ with sheaves on $x$ and identify their subobjects. Irreducibility of $E$ forces $\mathcal H^0Q=0$ or $i_{x*}E$. The displayed sequence and the two-degree heart description then give $Q=0$ or $R=0$, respectively. The object $i_{x*}E$ is nonzero since $i_x^*i_{x*}E=E\ne0$, so it is simple. In the Weil case the supported equivalence retains Frobenius and hence gives sub-Weil-modules of $E$.

Let $P=(j_*\mathcal N)[1]$ for nonzero irreducible lisse $\mathcal N$, and let $0\to Q\to P\to R\to0$ be exact in the heart. Parts (3)--(5) of [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart] give $\mathcal H^0R=0$ and
$$0\to A\to j_*\mathcal N\xrightarrow{f}B\to T_0\to0,$$
where $A=\mathcal H^{-1}Q$, $B=\mathcal H^{-1}R$ have no punctual subsheaf and $T_0=\mathcal H^0Q$ is punctual. Choose $k:U'\hookrightarrow U$ making $A,B$ lisse and $T_0$ zero, using [sk-lem-coefficient-heart], and put $j'=jk$. Exact restriction from [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology] gives
$$0\to A|_{U'}\to\mathcal N|_{U'}\to B|_{U'}\to0.$$
By Step 2, $\mathcal N|_{U'}$ is irreducible (also in the Weil lisse category). Its lisse subobject $A|_{U'}$ is therefore zero or the whole sheaf.

source.place: Middle extensions are simple: six-term sequence and restriction to a common dense open

proof.text:
Suppose $A|_{U'}=0$ in Step 6. Then $A$ is punctual and hence zero. The restriction of $f$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal N|_{U'}\cong B|_{U'}$. By Step 3, the unit $u:B\to j'_*j'^*B$ is monic. Naturality of the ordinary adjunction of [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology] identifies $uf$, through that restricted isomorphism, with the unit
$$j_*\mathcal N\longrightarrow j'_*k^*\mathcal N=j_*k_*k^*\mathcal N.$$
The equality of direct images follows directly from their section formula; this unit is $j_*$ of the lisse unit in Step 2, hence is an isomorphism. Thus $u$ is both monic and split epic: a right inverse is $f(uf)^{-1}$. Consequently $u$ and $f$ are isomorphisms, $T_0=0$, and $Q=0$ by [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart](3). This proves the boundary-subobject exclusion without citing the proof of another node.

source.place: Middle-extension paragraph (a): the composite of units and the vanishing of Q

proof.text: Suppose instead that $A|_{U'}=\mathcal N|_{U'}$. Then $B|_{U'}=0$, so $B$ is punctual. By [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart](3) it has no punctual subsheaf, hence $B=0$. Together with $\mathcal H^0R=0$ this gives $R=0$. These two cases exhaust the subobjects of $P$. Since $j^*j_*\mathcal N=\mathcal N\ne0$, $P\ne0$, and $P$ is simple.

source.place: Middle-extension paragraph (b), completing simplicity of middle extensions

proof.text:
Now let $P$ be any simple object of the heart. Part (5) of [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart] gives
$$0\to(\mathcal H^{-1}P)[1]\to P\to(\mathcal H^0P)[0]\to0.$$
Its two outer terms cannot both be nonzero. Thus either $P=\mathcal G[0]$ for a nonzero punctual sheaf $\mathcal G$, or $P=\mathcal F[1]$ for a nonzero sheaf $\mathcal F$ with no punctual subsheaf. These are precisely the two cases allowed by part (3).

source.place: Every simple object is of one of the two kinds: canonical short exact sequence

proof.text: In the punctual case, let $Z$ be the finite reduced closed support. By [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], $\mathcal G=i_*i^*\mathcal G$. As $Z=\coprod_{x\in Z}x$, a sheaf on $Z$ is a tuple of sheaves on its components: sections over an object over $Z$ are the product of the sections over its disjoint component pieces, by the sheaf gluing axiom. A finite product is also a direct sum here. Hence $\mathcal G=\bigoplus_{x\in Z}i_{x*}E_x$. Every subsheaf $\mathcal G'$ and the quotient $\mathcal G/\mathcal G'$ are punctual. Their ordinary short exact sequence gives a distinguished triangle by [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](4) for the standard heart, and all three terms belong to the perverse heart by [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart](3),(4). The same triangle is therefore short exact in the perverse heart by the cited clause (4). Simplicity forces exactly one nonzero summand, and forces its $E_x$ to have no proper nonzero subsheaf. Thus $P=i_{x*}E_x$ with $E_x$ irreducible. For Weil pairs take $Z_0$ as the finite reduced support over $k_0$ and decompose by its closed points, keeping each Frobenius orbit together. The same argument uses Step 4 and gives an irreducible Weil module on that closed point.

source.place: Classification: the punctual case and the finite supported decomposition

proof.text:
In the other case, choose a dense lisse open $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ for $\mathcal F$ by [sk-lem-coefficient-heart], and put $\mathcal N=j^*\mathcal F$. The unit $\mathcal F\to j_*\mathcal N$ is monic by Step 3 and has punctual cokernel $B_0$, by exact restriction in [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology]. In particular $\mathcal N\ne0$. The resulting ordinary short exact sequence gives, by [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](4) and rotation, the geometric triangle
$$B_0[0]\to\mathcal F[1]\to(j_*\mathcal N)[1]\to B_0[1].$$
All three terms are perverse by [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart](3),(4), so clause (4) of the same heart-triangle lemma makes the first three terms short exact in the perverse heart. In the Weil case its last two maps are equivariant ordinary unit maps shifted by one; the first term, as their kernel, inherits the given Weil structure on $B_0$ by naturality of standard cohomology, or equivalently by the kernel universal property of Step 4. The quotient $(j_*\mathcal N)[1]$ is nonzero. Simplicity forces $B_0=0$, and $P=(j_*\mathcal N)[1]$.

source.place: Classification: the sheaf unit and its punctual cokernel

proof.text: It remains to prove that $\mathcal N$ in Step 11 is irreducible. Suppose $0\ne\mathcal N'\subsetneq\mathcal N$ is a lisse subobject, equivariant in the Weil case. By [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2), lisse sheaves form an exact abelian category on each connected component, so $L=\mathcal N/\mathcal N'$ is lisse and nonzero. The same is true for the equivariant quotient by Step 4. Ordinary $j_*$ is a right adjoint by [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], so it preserves this monomorphism. Let $B$ be the constructible cokernel of $j_*\mathcal N'\to j_*\mathcal N$. Exact restriction gives $B|_U=L$. Choose a dense $v:V\hookrightarrow C$, with $V\subseteq U$, on which $B$ is lisse, using [sk-lem-coefficient-heart].

source.place: Classification: a putative lisse subobject and the ordinary cokernel

proof.text:
Define $B''=\operatorname{im}(B\to v_*v^*B)$ and $F'=\ker(j_*\mathcal N\to B'')$. These are constructible by the abelian closure and constructibility in [sk-lem-coefficient-heart, lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology]. The composite onto $B''$ is epic, giving
$$0\to F'\to j_*\mathcal N\to B''\to0.$$
The target $v_*v^*B$ has no punctual subsheaf by Step 3, so neither does $B''$. Nor does $F'$, since it is a subsheaf of $j_*\mathcal N$. On $V$, $B''|_V=B|_V=L|_V$ and $F'|_V=\mathcal N'|_V$. Both are nonzero: a nonzero lisse sheaf has positive rank on at least one component, and a dense open meets that component. Thus $F'$ and $B''$ are both nonzero. This is the source's saturation construction written directly as the image of a unit, so no assertion about an uncited largest punctual subsheaf is needed. All the maps are natural and hence equivariant when the input is Weil.

source.place: Classification: saturation; replacing the unnamed maximal-punctual-subsheaf assertion by an explicit kernel and image

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](4) in the standard geometric heart, the exact sheaf sequence of Step 13 gives a distinguished triangle after shifting by one. All three shifted sheaves are perverse by [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart](3), because they have no punctual subsheaf. Apply clause (4) of the heart-triangle lemma to the perverse t-structure: this gives
$$0\to F'[1]\to(j_*\mathcal N)[1]\to B''[1]\to0$$
in the perverse heart. In the Weil case the first two maps are already equivariant and Step 4 gives the same exact sequence of pairs. Its two outer objects are nonzero by Step 13, contradicting simplicity of $P$. Thus $\mathcal N$ is irreducible. Steps 5--8 prove that both listed kinds are simple; Steps 9--14 prove that every simple belongs to the list.

source.place: Classification: the saturated subobject contradiction and conclusion
